say: For I30, the missing doorway is delivery: can a venue automatically attach updated cards to booking confirmations? Otherwise we’re building a sign nobody walks past.
When I design a screen I remove anything that competes with the main action. I31 needs one play button, not an events feed.
Guys, listen, I back I31 because we can test repeat use for €20 without selling students another subscription. Four voluntary returns earns another experiment, not a sponsor pitch.

Eurostat reports rising EU rents, not a Riga rental-search problem. Before pitching an automated listing scout, I’d need a permitted local feed and evidence students repeatedly miss suitable listings.

Let me push back on my own I30: we have a restriction, not recurring demand, so I’m withdrawing it. I32’s hypothetical €10/month exceeds my €8 lunch; what does material matching save an instructor that free project libraries don’t?
I30 “Before the Curtain” is dropped: withdrawn by Dominykas.
I32 would convince me if instructors choose matched cards over their usual free resources twice. Time saved matters, but so does whether children actually enjoy making the thing.
Dominykas, matching must save preparation time, not merely generate crafts. I’d compare against instructors’ usual free resources; if they prefer those twice, I32 fails.
For I32, count safety-review minutes as preparation time too. Saving instructors ten minutes by giving ourselves twenty is outsourcing, not a loop.

I32 needs a NO-PURCHASE rule: missing materials must trigger another checked project, not a shopping list. I’d consider backing after instructors choose those cards twice over their usual free resources.
For I32, I’d want the person controlling the activity budget in the pilot, not just enthusiastic instructors. Can we invite provider managers alongside them?
I oppose I32 for now: why daily projects if instructors plan weekly? We haven’t established a repeat-use rhythm that justifies the extra safety checks.
I back I31 for the free pilot: ninety seconds feels manageable. Please check Riga place-name pronunciation before publishing; accurate scripts can still become misleading audio.
